records.conditions: Different model generations; source lists 128k input tokens for each, in publisher notation.
records.implication: Persist selected dimension and model identity with the index. Do not transfer v5's default to v4 or assume equal dimension means equal embedding space.

records.semantics: endpoint batch/size limits and default truncation
records.quantity: batch size; image payload; overlength handling
records.value: texts: 96; inputs: 96; v4+ images combined: 20 MB; truncate default END
records.conditions: Current v2 reference does not impose an image-count limit for v4+; older v1 guide states up to 96 v4 images. Treat parameter/API version and image bytes separately. NONE returns an overlength error.
records.implication: Never present successful default truncation as preservation of every input token. Avoid one brand-wide image-count cap.

records.value: 32, 000 per text; at most 1, 000 texts; aggregate 120K / 320K / 1M tokens respectively
records.conditions: Selected output dimension 1024(default), 256, 512 or 2048. Do not infer missing voyage-code-4 batch semantics from voyage-code-3.
records.implication: Check both item and batch budgets. Splitting a batch does not repair a too-long individual item.

records.semantics: documented default transform and packed output layout
records.quantity: truncation policy and binary storage length
records.value: truncation=true by default; false raises overlength error; binary/ubinary returned integer-list length = output_dimension / 8
records.conditions: Applicable model/dtype support remains source-specific; the logical vector dimension is not the returned packed-list length.
records.implication: Store the effective transform and logical dimension/dtype. Do not interpret a 128-element packed result as a 128-dimensional float vector.

records.semantics: conditional total/chunk limits and default target
records.value: 32, 000 per chunk; 120, 000 total with auto-chunking, otherwise 32, 000; target chunk default 512
records.conditions: The overview footnote uses enable_auto_chunk while the SDK signature uses enable_auto_chunking. Target chunk size/overlap are upper bounds, not guaranteed exact segmentation; custom client chunk_fn cannot combine with server auto-chunking.
records.implication: Pin SDK/server parameter mapping and actual returned chunk_texts. A larger total window does not enlarge every chunk.

records.value: card: 32K sequence; pinned config max_position_embeddings=32768; dimensions 32..1024; example max_length=8192
records.conditions: The example's truncation limit is not the card's model ceiling. Configuration and card do not establish runtime quality/admission at every length.
records.implication: Record the actual preprocessing limit and selected dimension separately from the model's published/configured capacity.

records.semantics: published sequence limit and multiple retrieval representations
records.value: 8192 input tokens; dense dimension 1024; dense, sparse and multi-vector outputs
records.conditions: Example max_passage_length=128 is a configured speed/length choice, not the published model maximum.
records.implication: Require the consumer's dense/sparse/late-interaction representation support, in addition to length and any dimension check.

records.route: pinned card and Sentence Transformers dense-layer config
records.semantics: multi-vector projection versus variable sequence shape
records.value: out_features=128; card example query (28, 128) and document (1030, 128)
records.unit: vector dimensions per token/patch; example sequence lengths
records.conditions: 28 and 1030 are illustrated shapes, not universal token/patch counts. The card documents MaxSim late interaction and processor-prefix differences across engine versions.
records.implication: A single-vector dimension equality check cannot certify compatibility. Pin processor/runtime and score method as part of retrieval identity.

records.semantics: documented truncation behavior and task formatting
records.value: long texts truncated to at most 512 tokens
records.conditions: Card FAQ requires task-appropriate query/passage prefixes; input formatting is separate from the retained sequence cap.
records.implication: Keep preprocessing/prefix policy and truncation visible. Do not market unchanged handling of longer documents.

records.value: 32768 sequence; dense default 2048, selectable 128/256/512/1024/2048; multi-vector width 128
